title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1RC---_0RD0RE_1LE0RB_0LA0LF_0RC0LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1RC---_0RD0RE_1LE0RB_0LA0LF_0RC0LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its run is a bouncer that works in phases; within a phase it is completely regular, and that part is proved in Lean for every size. The open part is what happens between phases. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves, by the kernel alone, the rule of the main regime for all sizes (three round trips of the head turn P a (b+3) into P (a+6) (b+1)) and that the run from blank tape enters it; the end of a phase, and the nested phases that appear after 107 steps, are only observed. No halt in the first 109 steps (C), 3·1011 with a macro simulator.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The main regime, for all sizes
claims.text: Write P a b for the tape F>0^6 (1000)^a 1 0 1 1 1 (0001)^b 0 1 0 0 0 1 0 1 0 0 0 0 1 (blank on both sides). Three round trips of the head take P a (b+3) to P (a+6) (b+1) in 114a + 114b + 1115 steps, for every a and b; iterated, P a (b+2k+1) reaches P (a+6k) (b+1). The one-cycle trace is written by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py and checked by the kernel; the re-bracketing and the induction are hand-written.

claims.title: The run enters the main regime
claims.text: After 30,224 steps from blank tape the configuration is exactly P 13 27 (list simulator, evaluated by the kernel), so the run passes through P (13+6k) (27−2k) and reaches P 91 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 33,368 cells have been visited and 12,501 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.478). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501).

claims.title: No halt in the first 3·10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 4 cells, runs of equal blocks crossed at once) runs 3·1011 steps without a halt; at the end the tape has three long segments, 1111^26184 … 1000^24523 … 0010^91400.
claims.where: the run behind this page (a C macro simulator in the style of tools/py/bbtools/macro.py)

claims.title: B never reads a 1 (so far)
claims.text: The machine halts only in B reading a 1, and B is entered from A>0 (writing 1, moving right) or from D>1. In the first 108 steps B is entered 13,163,946 times and reads a 0 every time.
claims.where: a transition counter run over the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps

claims.title: Phases that roughly triple
claims.text: A phase starts at F>0^6 (1000)^3 1 0 1 1 1 (0001)^b …. The successive starting values are b = 0, 2, 6, 32, 94, 287, 862 (steps 613 to 10,800,216): during a phase the left part grows by 6 blocks while the right loses 2, so it ends with about 3b blocks of 1000, and these become the next phase's 0001s. After b = 862 the rebuild is incomplete and a second segment (1000)^859 stays to the right; the next phases (b = 8, 36, 290, 1156) eat it slowly (859, 850, 742, 454). The phase map depends on which of three tail shapes is current when the 0001s run out, an arithmetic (Collatz-like) dependence that is not analysed yet.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would have to follow the phase ends: what each of the three tail shapes does when the last 0001 is eaten, and how the nested segments are rebuilt.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LD_0RC0RF_1LD0RB_1LE---_0LA0LB_0LE0RA up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine bounces back and forth across a tape of 4-cell blocks, and its run comes in phases: inside a phase every round trip does the same thing (proved in Lean for every size), and at the end of a phase the tape is rebuilt about three times bigger. Whether some phase end goes wrong is the open question.

facts.text: The main-regime rule P a (b+3) → P (a+6) (b+1), proved by the kernel.
No halt in a macro simulator; 10<sup>9</sup> in the plain C simulator.
Phase lengths b = 0, 2, 6, 32, 94, 287, 862, then nested phases.

sections.heading: The one way to halt
html: The table has one halting entry: state B reading a 1. B is entered in two ways: A reads a 0, writes a 1 and moves right (A>0 1 halts at once), or D reads a 1, writes a 0 and moves right (D>1 1 halts). So the machine halts exactly when, at one of these two moments, the cell to the right of the head holds a 1.

In the first 108 steps B is entered more than 13 million times and always finds a 0. Most of these entries happen inside the long sweeps, where the blocks around the head are fixed words, so they are safe by construction; the danger is concentrated at the two ends of the tape, where the head turns.

sections.heading: The main regime: blocks of four cells
html: Stop the simulator each time the head stands at the left end of the tape in state F. Most of the time the tape then reads
where T, the tail, is one of three short words that take turns: 0 1 0 0 0 1 0 1 0 0 0 0 1, 0 1 0 1 1 0 1 0 0 0 0 1 and 0 1 1 1 0 1 1. One round trip of the head does this:

• Moving right, a pair of 0s travels with the head (state D) and turns every block into solid ones: 0 0 D>1 0 0 0 becomes 1 1 1 1 0 0 D>, 28 steps per block, and the 0001 blocks likewise. Halfway through a sweep the whole tape looks like 1^(4a+…) 0 0 0 1^(4b+1) ….
• At the right end the tail changes to the next of its three shapes, and on two shapes of three it swallows one block 0001.
• Moving left, state A turns the ones back into blocks: 1 1 1 1 A>1 becomes A>1 0 0 0 1, 10 steps per block, which, read from the other end, is again 1000.
• At the left end a short dance (states F, D, A, E) writes two more blocks 1000.

So three round trips take a = 13, b = 27 to a = 19, b = 25. Lean proves this for every a and b: with P a b the tape above with the first tail, P a (b+3) becomes P (a+6) (b+1) in 114a + 114b + 1115 steps (P_step), and by induction P a (b+2k+1) becomes P (a+6k) (b+1) (P_iter). The run from blank tape is exactly P 13 27 after 30,224 steps (reach_P), so for the next 13 rounds of three trips nothing can go wrong.

sections.heading: Phases, each about three times the last
html: A regime like this cannot last: the 0001 blocks run out. Then the tail meets the solid part, the head carries a message to the left, and the tape is reorganised: the left blocks, about 3b of them, become the right reservoir of the next phase, and the left part starts again from (1000)^3. The phases start with

at steps 613, 1,279, 3,045, 22,299, 150,253, 1,249,630 and 10,800,216 (py/phases.py). The factor is about 3, but the offsets (32 = 3·6 + 14, 94 = 3·32 − 2, 287 = 3·94 + 5) depend on which tail shape is current when the reservoir runs out: an arithmetic dependence of the kind that makes a machine Collatz-like.

After the phase with b = 862 the rebuild is incomplete: a second segment (1000)^859 stays behind on the right, and the next phases start at b = 8, 36, 290, 1156 while that segment shrinks to 850, 742, 454. So the long run is a nest of counters, a segment being used up as fuel by the phases inside it. At 3·1011 steps the tape has three long segments. Whether the machine halts depends on whether some phase end ever leaves a 1 to the right of A>0 or D>1, and that needs the phase ends worked out in general, which is the next step.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.478). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501).
After 109 steps the tape spans 33,368 cells (14,776 left of the start, 9,583 right), with a density of 1s of 0.375.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Two-sided bouncer on blocks 1000 | 0001: each round trip adds 1000s on the left and the right end eats a 0001 on two trips of three; when the 0001s run out the tape is rebuilt with about three times as many (main regime proved for all sizes).
family: two-sided bouncer, words 1000 | 0001, phases that roughly triple
